summary: The run demonstrates the intended command-driven sequence through fill, 10 s wait, transfer, STOP pause, START resume, second 10 s wait, drain, and return to idle, and it also responds to SHUT by inhibiting the inlet and moving to a shutdown state. Specifically, START at 10 s leads to inlet opening at 10.1 s, Tank 1 reaches high level at 60.1 s, transfer begins at 70.1 s after a 10 s wait, STOP at 80.0 s closes the transfer at 80.1 s and pauses in state 7, START at 200.0 s resumes transfer at 200.1 s, Tank 1 reaches low at 235.1 s, drain begins at 245.1 s after another 10 s wait, and Tank 2 reaches low at 285.1 s so the controller returns to state 1. However, the SHUT behavior required by the brief is not fully demonstrated: when SHUT is issued at 500.0 s, both tanks are already at their low levels with final levels 0.1 and 0.1, so the run does not actually show SHUT opening transfer and drain until both tanks become empty from a nonempty condition.
issues: The brief says SHUT opens the transfer and drain paths until both tanks are empty, but at the actual SHUT event t=500.0000000000452 neither transfer nor drain opens: controller.transferOpen stays 0 for the rest of the run, controller.drainOpen stays 0 for the rest of the run, transferValve.qCmd final=0, and drainValve.qCmd final=0.

The run does not demonstrate SHUT emptying nonempty tanks. At t=500 s the tanks are already at their modeled low condition: tank1.lowReached=1 since t=235.1000000078125 and tank2.lowReached=1 since t=285.1000000211651. Their final levels remain tank1.level=0.1 and tank2.level=0.1, so no further emptying occurs after SHUT.

The brief's SHUT requirement says transfer and drain paths are opened until both tanks are empty, but the actual final levels are not zero: tank1 final=0.1 and tank2 final=0.1. In this model, 'empty' is effectively treated as the low-level threshold rather than zero inventory.
assumptions: Numeric values were assumed for tank cross-sectional area, high-level threshold, low-level threshold, initial levels, nominal inlet flow, nominal transfer flow, nominal drain flow, command schedule times, pulse widths, controller scan period, and experiment interval/tolerance because the source note did not provide them.

Valve routing was assumed as signal-flow only: inlet adds to Tank 1, transfer removes from Tank 1 and adds the same flow to Tank 2, and drain removes from Tank 2; this routing is not explicit in the source note.

The confirmed shared low-level switch was implemented as two Boolean inputs to the controller, one representing low detection on Tank 1 during transfer completion and one representing low detection on Tank 2 during drain completion.

The autonomous command schedule was assumed so the model would demonstrate START, STOP/resume, and SHUT within 900 s; the actual schedule used includes START pulses at about 10 s and 200 s, a STOP pulse at about 80 s, and a SHUT pulse at about 500 s.

From the trajectory itself, the model assumes low level corresponds to a remaining liquid level of 0.1 rather than zero, because tank1.lowReached becomes 1 at 0.1 and tank2.lowReached becomes 1 at 0.1, and both tanks stay at 0.1 afterward.

From the observed timing and flow magnitudes, the model assumes constant commanded flows of 0.02 level-units per second with effectively unit tank area: Tank 1 rises from 0.1 to 1.0 in 50 s of filling, falls from 1.0 to 0.8 in 10 s of transfer before STOP, then from 0.8 to 0.1 in 35 s after resume; Tank 2 rises from 0.1 to 0.3 in the first 10 s of transfer, then to 1.0 by the end of resumed transfer, and drains back to 0.1 over 40 s.
root_causes: SHUT was commanded only after the normal cycle had already completed and both low-level conditions were true. The event trace shows the controller returned to state 1 at t=285.1000000211651 after draining Tank 2, and SHUT was not issued until t=500.0000000000452. Because there was no remaining transfer or drain work to do under the model's low-level-based logic, SHUT only changed controller.sequenceState to 9 and set inletInhibited=1; it did not produce transferOpen or drainOpen events.

The model's completion logic for transfer and drain is tied to low-level switches rather than zero tank level. tank1.lowReached switches to 1 at t=235.1000000078125 and tank2.lowReached switches to 1 at t=285.1000000211651, both with final levels of 0.1. As soon as those Boolean conditions become true, the controller advances and then closes the valves, leaving 0.1 in each tank. That is why the run can satisfy the modeled sequence yet fail the brief's literal 'both tanks are empty' wording.

The chosen autonomous command schedule prevented an informative shutdown test. By placing SHUT at 500 s, long after the drain finished at 285.1 s, the simulation never exercised the stated override behavior 'open transfer and drain until both tanks are empty' from a nonempty operating state. This is not a solver problem; it is a consequence of the assumed command timing used to generate the demonstration.
